title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.230): f: S -> T, with S (smooth?) relative over T. E is a locally free O_S-module with a stratification relative to T, i.e. an integrable connection with all higher Taylor data. The formal Poincaré lemma is assumed for the de Rham complex Omega^*_{S/T}(E) = E ⊗ Omega^*_{S/T}, for instance when S/T is smooth in characteristic 0. P is a quasi-coherent O_S-module. Diff^i(E,P) = Hom_{O_S}(P^i(E),P) is the sheaf of differential operators of order <= i, in the sense of EGA IV 16.

Page 230 established an exact sequence
0 <- Hom(E,P) <- Diff^i(E,P) <- Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Omega^1,P) <- Diff^{i-2}(E⊗Omega^2,P) <- ...
The first map is u |-> u∘delta_i, where delta_i: E -> P^i(E) is the 'horizontal Taylor expansion' given by the stratification. The next maps are composition with d^0_E, d^1_E, and so on. Diff^i_+(E,P) is the kernel of the first map. These are the operators 'with constant coefficients relative to the stratification', i.e. those that kill the formal horizontal sections.

This page, step by step:
(i) Corollary. Exactness at the next two spots gives
Diff^i_+(E,P) ≅ Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Omega^1,P) / Im Diff^{i-2}(E⊗Omega^2,P).
In words, an order-<= i operator killing horizontal sections factors as v∘d^0_E, with v of order <= i-1 and unique modulo operators of the form w∘d^1_E.
(ii) Restriction map. Sending u = v∘d^0 to v restricted to the sheaf of closed forms Ker d^1_E gives an additive map Diff^i_+(E,P) -> Homadd(Ker d^1_E, P). It is well defined because w∘d^1 vanishes on Ker d^1. Grothendieck marks injectivity with '(?)'. He then defines the image as the sheaf of 'differential operators from Ker d^1_E to P'. Note that Ker d^1_E is only an f^{-1}O_T-module, not an O_S-module, so this extends the notion of differential operator to such sheaves via the de Rham complex.
(iii) Representing object. For fixed i, the representing ('universal') target for constant-coefficient operators of order <= i is P^i(E) / O_S·delta_i(E). Operators in Diff^i_+ are exactly the linear maps P^i(E) -> P killing delta_i(E).
(iv) Part 3. Take a submodule N ⊂ E and set M = E/N. Grothendieck considers 'differential' maps Ker d^1_E -> P that vanish on d^0_E(N). These correspond to:
- operators E -> P of order <= i that kill N, hence
- operators M -> P which are 'directly' of order <= i on E, hence
- linear maps P^i(M) -> P killing rho_i(E), where rho_i is the composite E -> P^i(E) -> P^i(M).
The next page assembles P_i = P^i(M)/O_S·rho_i(E) into a strict projective system determined by M and rho_infinity: E -> P^infinity(M). The conditions on rho_infinity are that its composite to M be an epimorphism, plus integrability.

In modern terms, rho_infinity is the horizontal (D-linear) map E -> J^infinity(M) that corresponds, under the adjunction Hom_O(E,M) = Hom_D(E, J^infinity M), to the projection E -> M. The aim, in the Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs context, seems to be an intrinsic jet-theoretic description of the differential operators that annihilate classes in relative de Rham cohomology, namely Picard–Fuchs-type operators: closed forms modulo exact ones, presented as a quotient of a stratified module.
errors: The '(?)' on injectivity is unnecessary. If v vanishes on Ker d^1_E, it vanishes on Im d^0_E ⊂ Ker d^1_E, so u = v∘d^0_E = 0. The map is injective with no further hypothesis.
Minor redundancy: delta_i (and rho_i on the next page) is O_S-linear for the structure used to define Diff, so O_S·delta_i(E) is just delta_i(E). The 'O_S·' is harmless.

Subtle point not made explicit: Zariski-locally Ker d^1 ≠ Im d^0 (relative H^1_dR). The 'differential operators on Ker d^1' therefore carry the extension v from Im d^0 to closed forms as data. The correspondence is with classes of v, not with operators on Im d^0 alone. The text is consistent with this but does not comment on it.

ideas.what: Operators killing horizontal sections of a stratified module factor through the de Rham differential, with an order shift, by the formal Poincaré lemma; corollary computing Diff^i_+ as a quotient of Diff^{i-1}(E⊗Omega^1,P).
ideas.modern_name: Dual (Spencer-type) resolution / jet-theoretic formal Poincaré lemma; de Rham complex vs. Spencer complex duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Spencer, Goldschmidt (linear PDE); Grothendieck–Berthelot–Illusie for crystalline/linearization versions (Berthelot 1974, Grothendieck 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' 1968)
ideas.where_published: Closely related linearization of differential operators in Grothendieck's IHES notes 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and EGA IV §16.

ideas.what: Defining 'differential operators' from the sheaf of closed forms Ker d^1_E (only an f^{-1}O_T-module) to an O_S-module, as images of constant-coefficient operators.
ideas.modern_name: Differential operators on non-O-module sheaves via de Rham resolution; related to f^{-1}O_T-linear differential operators in Gauss–Manin theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; implicit in Katz–Oda (1968) and Berthelot style treatments of Gauss–Manin

ideas.what: Universal target P^i(E)/O_S·delta_i(E) for constant-coefficient operators; for a quotient M = E/N, the system P^i(M)/O_S·rho_i(E) determined by rho_infinity: E -> P^infinity(M).
ideas.modern_name: Infinite jet module J^infinity(M) as co-induced D-module; adjunction Hom_O(E,M) = Hom_D(E, J^infinity M); prolongation of a linear PDE system
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard D-module/jet theory (Spencer, Goldschmidt, Malgrange; Kashiwara for D-modules)
ideas.where_published: Principal parts P^i are from EGA IV 16.3–16.8.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a jet-theoretic, intrinsic notion of 'differential operator on the sheaf of closed relative forms Ker d^1_E' and of operators on M = E/N that are 'directly' of order <= i on E. This is apparently meant to describe Picard–Fuchs operators via P^infinity(M) with integrability conditions. The thread breaks off on the next page ('+ conditions d'intégrabilité ---') and is not developed in this form in known published texts. Mathematically it is subsumed by standard D-module theory.
missed.quote: l'image est appelée faisceau des op. diff. de Ker d^1_E dans P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck approaching Picard–Fuchs equations via principal parts and duality of de Rham complexes, rather than via D-modules. No result is likely missing from the modern literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially routine homological algebra of differential operators (EGA IV principal parts plus formal Poincaré lemma). The slight novelty, operators defined on Ker d^1 as a non-O-module, is a natural device subsumed by later D-module theory.
transcription_corrections: 'P^{(i)}(E) / O_S . ∂_i(E)': in the image the superscript is plain i (P^i(E)). The map written ∂_i is the same as delta^E_i of p.230.
The quotient in the corollary reads 'Im Diff^{i-2}(E⊗Omega^2_{S/T}, P)'. The superscript n/2 on Omega is squeezed at the margin but is 2.
'(d'ordre ≤ i)' is written as an inserted parenthetical after 'd'ordre constants'.
In part 3 the phrase 'Ils (pour l'ordre ≤ i) correspondent aux homom. linéaires' has 'aux homom.' as a superscript insertion, consistent with the transcription.
